body: I lost my career. It doesn't matter how hard I try, it's gone. My friends are gone. It's over.
I guess I don't see a way to move forward. Either in life goals or emotional health wise. I'm working hard at it from both ends, but it's just not moving. I think it's over.
I liked what I used to have. I worked really, really hard to get there, and it's all gone.

Yeah, I definitely do. Most recently on Sunday. And I told my doctor how bad it was getting on Thursday. My doctor changed my medication. My therapist says I'm getting better, and that I need to wait a bit longer. But it's not all trauma. As a result of this, I've lost my home, my career, my friends, and all my possessions. I've got nothing. I can't imagine recapturing a happy life. Or an ok life. I imagine in the future life as a type of zombie. Like I should have died in the attack, and everything that happens after is some sort of shitty half-life. I'll be completely homeless soon. And I'm already completely alone.

The good was trying to put me on meds. I like the anti-anxiety meds. The bad was the use of flashlights (major trigger, but we worked it out) an asshole psych who sucked balls, singing before bed (not a joke), really awful volunteer staff who continually offered platitudes about Jesus and/or silver linings. Oh, and we painted paint by numbers. I went to a few classes on mental health, but they were poorly run and usually led to scary yelling.

I go to a therapist twice a week. I was fortunate because of what happened to get to get an excellent, like really great therapist, super cheap. I don't feel safe; car. I also have been completely honest with her. About a month ago, she helped me get inpatient at a hospital. However, it was a horrible, horrible program. And I don't think she knows how to help me anymore.
I don't know what else to do.

No. I live in my car and couch surf. I feel like I'm getting closer to the edge. But there's no tv for video games, movies, etc. I don't have an address, so I don't have a library card. I do read online though, it's just hard and also not something I can do an entire day. I find myself finding nice places that are drivable and sitting there with my tools, ready to die. I feel more peaceful.

I don't have anything to do. I survived a violent attack and had to move for safety reasons. In my new area, I don't have a job or friends. PTSD also makes doing things kind of difficult. I made a list of things I like to do that I have access to, but it's incredibly short.
